BACKGROUND
The property owner purchased the property five (5) years ago, opening Tonymoly after about a
year of renovations. However, since the pandemic, the property owner states that Tonymoly sales
declined nearly 50% with many customers purchasing items online through companies such as
Amazon. Therefore, the property owner is looking to change the business to something more
sustainable.

ANALYSIS
The applicant is requesting approval of a Planned Development Permit, Conditional Use Permit,
and a Variance to establish an educational center known as Eye Level Alhambra. The proposed
educational center will operate within an existing 1,197 square foot tenant space within an existing
2,458 square foot two-unit commercial building. The proposed education center will have
approximately three (3) staff members and operate between the hours of 2:00 pm and 7:00 pm,
Monday through Saturday.
Educational, Instructional and Tutoring Services are a conditionally permitted use in the CBD zone
pursuant to AMC Section 23.28.030(DD) [CPD Zone] of the Alhambra Municipal Code (AMC)
which requires Planning Commission approval. A Planned Development Permit is required
pursuant to Alhambra Municipal Code (AMC) Section 23.62.020(B)(4) since the proposed use
intensifies the parking from one (1) parking space for each 250 square feet (retail use) to one (1)
space for each 125 square feet (educational use) with a 10-space minimum, which is discussed in
further detail later in this report.

Eye Level Alhambra allows each child to become the key to his or her success. Students set goals
with the assistance of the instructor, work to keep the promises they make for themselves and
master the step-by-step curriculum. With each success, the student grows more confident,
motivated, and self-directed in the quest for knowledge. Each student will choose either the Math
Curriculum, the English Curriculum, or both. Each Curriculum provides students with two (2) to
three (3) booklets per week. During the session, the Instructor will provide a five (5) to 10 minutes
coaching session per student on weekly assigned booklets that need to be completed at home. Eye
Level Alhambra will operate in a low student-instructor ratio environment. The average student-
instructor ratio will be 3 to 1, and there will be two instructors, one for Math and another for
English, at a time with a manager. Therefore, on average, there will be six (6) to seven (7) students
and three (3) staff members at any given time.

 Parking Variance
The subject property was developed in 1947 with the building occupying a majority of the lot with
little available on-site parking. In 1947, the City did not require off-street parking spaces for
commercial uses and the property was developed accordingly, however, off-street parking began
to be required for commercial uses in 1952. Since the subject property does not comply with
current off-street parking requirements, the property is legal-nonconforming with respect to
parking.

The Alhambra Municipal Code’s current parking requirements are based on uses and their floor
areas. As presented in the parking table below, under the AMC §23.52: [Off-Street Parking and
Loading Standards], a tutoring and educational services business comprised of 1,197 square feet
shall provide a minimum of 10 parking spaces at a 1:125 ratio, while the previous use required a
minimum of five (5) parking spaces. The existing nail salon next door (106 South First Street)
requires a minimum of two (2) parking spaces for every barber/beauty station. The existing beauty
salon has a total of four (4) stations, which would require a minimum of eight (8) parking spaces.
The proposed site has a total of three (3) parking spaces for the two-unit commercial building.
Therefore, the property has a deficit of 15 on-site parking spaces, which is five (5) spaces more
than the prior existing uses.

Pursuant to Alhambra Municipal Code Section 23.52.060(F), the Planning Commission may grant

Parking Garage) has 115 public parking spaces and is approximately 64-feet from the project site.
City Parking Lot 16 is located on the east side of South 2nd Street just south of Main Street. Lot 16

ENVIRONMENTAL STATUS
This application is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act, Section
15301, Existing Facilities, Class 1(a) consisting of the permitting, licensing, and leasing involving

PUBLIC NOTICE

of the date this report was finalized.

PROJECT FINDINGS
The land use entitlements for the Commission consideration is a Planned Development,
Conditional Use Permit, and Variance. Pursuant to the Alhambra Municipal Code these
entitlements can be approved if the Planning Commission can make all of the findings in support
of the project:

Variance Findings

  application of the zoning ordinance deprives such property of privileges enjoyed by other
  properties in the vicinity and under the identical zoning classification;
  2. The granting of such Variance will not be detrimental to the public interest, safety, health
  or welfare, and will not be detrimental or injurious to the property or improvements in the
  vicinity and zone in which the property is located;
  3. The granting of such Variance will not be contrary to or in conflict with the general
  purposes and intent of the Zoning Ordinance, nor to the goals and programs of the General
  Plan; and
  4. The Variance request is consistent with the purpose and intent of the zone in which the site
  is located.

CONCLUSION
Eye Level Alhambra allows each student to set goals and master the step-by-step curriculum with
a low student-instructor ratio environment of 3 to 1. An educational center, such as Eye Level
Alhambra, is a conditionally permitted use within the CBD and DRD zone. Although the property
has a total of three (3) on-site parking spaces, a total of 394 public parking spaces are within 400-
feet of the project site and accessible to the project. Furthermore, the proposed educational center
will also continue to diversify the uses within the downtown area. Therefore, Staff recommends
approval of this project.

(Section 23.66.050 of the Alhambra Municipal Code) for the revision to Conditional Use Permit CUP-20-
02, the Planning Commission hereby determines as follows:

A.  The proposed use is one conditionally permitted within the subject zone and complies with all of the
  applicable provisions of the Zoning Ordinance:

  The existing restaurant is allowed by right and the approved Conditional Use Permit CUP-20-02
  currently allows the on-site sales of beer and wine, in conjunction with meal service at the restaurant
  is in compliance with the Central Business District-Downtown Revitalization District zone pursuant
  to AMC Section 23.26.030. The revision to CUP-20-02, changing the hours of operation to 7:00
  A.M.- 2:00 A.M. Monday through Sunday does not change the use, and the use will continue to
  comply with all applicable provisions of the Zoning Ordinance.

B.  The proposed use would not impair the integrity and character of the zone in which it is to be
  located:

  The proposed revision of CUP-20-02 allowing the change of hours of operation will not impair the
  integrity and character of the CBD-DRD (Central Business District-Downtown Revitalization
  District) zone. The existing restaurant use is presently serving beer and wine with meals and is
  operating responsibly as the City has not received any complaints about the business in relation to
  the beer and wine service. It is common for restaurants that serve beer and wine with meals to be
  open between the hours of 7:00AM -2:00AM in the City’s Downtown and other similar Downtown
  areas. In fact, there are nine (9) other restaurants within a two-block radius of the subject site that
  have similar business hours. Therefore, expanding the hours will be in conformance with the
  integrity and character of the CBD-DRD zone.

C.  The subject site is physically suitable for the type of land use being proposed:

  The revision of CUP-20-02 for the change of hours of operation will not affect the subject site’s
  physical suitability for the existing land use. The existing restaurant occupies a 1,924 square foot
  lease space. There will be no increase in the building area or building footprint as the current
  proposal only involves a change in business hours.

D.  The proposed use is compatible with the land uses presently on the subject property:

   The subject property is improved with an existing 3,040 square foot commercial building occupied
  by two (2) businesses: Yang’s Kitchen and Skateshop Pizza. Skateshop Pizza opens at 11:00 A.M.
  and closes at 8:00 P.M., daily. The extension of Yang’s Kitchen’s morning and evening business
  hours do not coincide with when Skateshop Pizza is open, therefore there would not be any
  compatibility concerns between the two business uses.

E.  The proposed use would be compatible with existing and future land uses within the zone and
  general area in which the proposed use is to be located:

  The proposed revision of hours of operation for the existing restaurant maintains the compatibility
  for the existing restaurant within the CBD-DRD zone and in the general area and it is anticipated
  that it will continue to be compatible with existing and future land uses that will locate in the
  immediate Downtown area. It is common for restaurants that serve beer and wine with meals to be
  open between the hours of 7:00AM -2:00AM in the Downtown area. In fact, there are nine (9) other
  restaurants within a two-block radius of the subject site that have similar business hours.

F.  There would be adequate provisions for water, sanitation, and public utilities and services to ensure
  that the proposed use would not be detrimental to public health and safety:

  The proposed revision of hours of operation for the previously entitled CUP-20-02 has been
  evaluated by the City’s Police and Fire departments which did not express concern and did not
  provide additional Conditions of Approval. There will continue to be adequate provisions for water,
  sanitation and public utilities and services for the occupants of the existing business.

G.  There would be adequate provisions for public access to serve the subject proposal:

  The project site is located along the Main Street corridor, one of the largest and most viable
  commercial districts in the City. Near the intersection of West Main Street and South 1st Street, the
  public access to the business will be through the main business entrance located on West Main
  Street. The property was developed in 1913 with no available on-site parking spaces. This is a legal
  nonconforming property with regards to parking requirements. However, nearby City-owned public
  parking lots are adequate and accessible to accommodate the existing restaurant. No additional
  parking is required for the proposed revisions to the business hours.

H.  The proposed use is consistent with the objectives, policies, general land uses and programs of the
  Alhambra General Plan:
